settings.title: Fruit
settings.body: Cold-steeped, dehydrated, roasted or reduced — whichever method gets the most out of it. Rarely juiced.

settings.title: Tannin
settings.body: Chamomile, cinnamon, tea, hops, citrus pith. Grip on the finish, so it holds a plate instead of washing through.

settings.title: Salinity
settings.body: Murray River salt, kombu. Salt makes food taste more like itself — a lever wine never had.

settings.title: Acidity
settings.body: Barossa verjus, citrus, vinegar. Resets the palate between bites, and cools chilli instead of stoking it.

settings.title: Not de-alcoholised
settings.body: No wine is made and then stripped. Nothing here has ever been fermented.

settings.title: Not a mocktail
settings.body: Mocktails are mixed to order and usually sweet. This is cooked in a facility and bottled dry.
Less water wasted than conventional beverage manufacturing.
Green energy across production, with carbon-neutral shipping.
Alcohol, in every bottle, from the first step to the last.

settings.title: Come and see it
settings.body: NONHQ is the world's first non-alcoholic cellar door. Taste the ingredients separately, then the bottles.

settings.title: Or start with a glass
settings.body: Tell the somm what you're eating and it will pick the bottle. That's the fastest version of everything on this page.
settings.label: Find your pairing

settings.title: Not an imitation
settings.body: It takes the seat wine had at the table. It doesn't try to taste like the thing that sat there.

settings.title: Preparation
settings.body: Whole fruit, herbs, spices, tea and verjus are sourced and prepped. Real produce, not concentrate.

settings.title: Cook
settings.body: Ingredients are cooked to build depth, texture and structure.

settings.title: Extraction
settings.body: Cold or hot, depending on the ingredient. Draws out flavour, colour and aromatics.

settings.title: Filter
settings.body: Solids are removed, leaving a clear, stable base liquid.

settings.title: Blend
settings.body: Filtered extracts are blended to the variant’s final flavour profile.

settings.title: Bottle
settings.body: The finished liquid is sent out for bottling.

settings.heading: We don't mimic wine. We make something else.
settings.lead: A chef-led drinks company in Melbourne, building wine alternatives out of real produce — fruit, tannin, salinity, acidity — and nothing that has ever been fermented.
settings.origin_heading: A drinks pairing in London that never left the restaurant.
settings.origin_body:
In 2017 Aaron Trotman was eating through Michelin-starred rooms in London. He took the alcohol pairing; the non-drinker at the table was handed something sweet and forgettable.

He had no background in drinks. He came from cosmetics chemistry, which turned out to matter more than a wine list would have. NON launched in 2019.
settings.quote: I thought it was a real shame that these drinks lived and died in fancy restaurants.
settings.pillars_heading: Every glass is built from four things
settings.origin_feature_alt: Dehydrated oranges lowered into the steep tank at NONHQ
settings.hard_image_alt: Spicing cherries by hand in the NON kitchen
settings.kitchen_caption: Every ingredient is processed on its own before anything is blended.

settings.label: Fruit
settings.title: Cooked, not fermented
settings.body: Whole fruit is steeped, roasted or dehydrated until the flavour concentrates. Nothing ferments and nothing is stripped out later.

settings.label: Tannin
settings.title: Grip, from leaves and skins
settings.body: Tea, chamomile, hops or skins go in for tannin — the drying grip that makes a drink feel like wine rather than juice.

settings.label: Salinity
settings.title: A pinch of salt
settings.body: Salt for salinity: the thing that makes a sip ask for the next one, and the reason these sit beside food.

settings.label: Acidity
settings.title: Verjus, not vinegar
settings.body: Unripe Semillon grapes from the Barossa, pressed into verjus. Acidity with none of the sharpness vinegar would bring.

settings.label: Balance
settings.title: Tasted to level
settings.body: Sugar goes in last and only as far as the fruit needs. Balance is judged in the kitchen, by tasting.
